---
title: "Teaching"
---

I teach courses in microeconomic theory, introductory economics, and the
history and development of economic thought at Hunter College and the
Graduate Center, CUNY. Below are selected course materials and resources
that I use in teaching.

## Graduate Microeconomic Theory

My graduate microeconomics materials emphasize strategic interaction,
information, and computational approaches to economic theory.

::: {.paper}
### Microeconomics II

Topics include principal-agent problems, bargaining, global games,
adverse selection, and related applications of game theory.

[Micro II Sandbox](https://github.com/mbaker21231/MicroII-Sandbox)
:::

## Introductory Economics

For introductory economics at Hunter, I use a variety of examples,
data, graphical exercises, and supplementary materials to connect basic
economic models to real-world questions.

::: {.paper}
### ECO 100 — Introduction to Economics

Jonathan Conning has assembled a useful collection of notes and teaching
resources for ECO 100 at Hunter.

[ECO 100 Resources](https://github.com/jhconning/eco100)
:::

## Development of Economic Thought

This course examines the development of economic ideas in their historical
and intellectual context, from early political economy through the
development of modern economics.

::: {.paper}
### History of Economic Thought Resources

The History of Economic Thought Website is an extensive reference for
economists, schools of thought, original texts, essays, and related
historical material.

[History of Economic Thought Website](https://www.hetwebsite.net/het/)
:::
